She was smoking her cigarette on the hospital balcony. She would always give Karen some of her cigarettes when she could. Karen had been with the hospital less than a year. She had not gotten any of Sarah's cigarettes yet though. She was waiting until the end of the shift.

Karen had been on duty that night since 20:00 and there had only been two incidents all night. A guy tried to start a fight with another patient, but Sarah stopped him before anyone was hurt. One of the patients, Bob, tried to commit suicide, and Karen helped stop him.

"Bob tried again didn't he?" she said looking up at Sarah from her desk.

"Yeah," said Sarah, "he said he was going to do something, so I got to him before he did it."

"You know if that happened in the real world, he might be a murderer?"

"What? Why would he be a murderer?" asked Sarah, who was still smoking her cigarette.

"I don't know," said Karen. "He might think that he has a right to kill someone because he stopped them from killing themselves." 

"Or someone else," added Sarah.

Sarah put her cigarette down, "That's a really weird thing to say. He can't come into the hospital and just do whatever he wants. He doesn't have a right to kill anyone just because they killed themselves."

"But you heard him," said Karen.
